blockers.description: UNDECLARED, UNPINNED behaviour change created by this branch, moving AWAY from bash, in the slot's own defect class: the operand-less named-fd redirect spellings `{v}<<` and `{v}<<<`. Adding ('<<<',HERE_STRING)/('<<-',HEREDOC_STRIP)/('<<',HEREDOC) to the named-fd operator table in /Users/pwilson/src/psh/psh/lexer/recognizers/operator.py#_try_var_fd_redirect changes what the session does with the DEGENERATE form (operator present, delimiter/word absent). At a real terminal, base and bash both COMPLETE the line with a syntax error and run the next command; the tip drops to PS2 and swallows the next physical line into the buffer — the exact 'psh says INCOMPLETE where bash says COMPLETE and eats the following line' shape MEDIUM-3 exists to close. Non-interactively rc/stdout are unchanged but the diagnostic text AND column change on all three channels and both parsers. This axis (operator present / operand missing) is absent from BOTH the named-fd differential battery (/Users/pwilson/src/psh/tests/unit/io_redirect/test_named_fd_heredoc.py — its only control is `{v}</dev/null`) and the PTY module (/Users/pwilson/src/psh/tests/system/interactive/test_heredoc_detection_interactive_pty.py — `named_fd_plain_redirect` is `{v}<`, never `{v}<<` bare). It is the fourth occurrence of the ruling-R9 pattern the integrator has already bounced three times: when a fix adds a decider arm, the arm's whole input space is the universe. It also falsifies an in-ledger claim: B44 states 'The round-3 diagnostic delta on `{v}<<<` is subsumed ... the diverging diagnostic no longer exists' — true for `{v}<<<hello`, FALSE for `{v}<<<` with no word, where the diverging diagnostic remains AND a new completeness divergence appeared. Brief §7 is explicit: any behaviour delta beyond the chartered fix must be probed vs live bash, both parsers, DECLARED + PINNED; an unpinned improvement is already a bounce, and this one is a regression relative to both base and the oracle.
